transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, but... well, honestly, what made me finally make an appointment is that I've been having this little issue at work. 

I'm in advertising sales, and we have these really long strategy meetings. I know I’m supposed to just stay seated and, you know, be professional, but I just keep getting up. I try to be really quiet and polite about it—usually I just make an excuse to go refill my water or I'll just sort of pace over by the printer for a second. It's probably not a huge deal, but I just can't seem to stay in my chair when I'm supposed to. 

Is that... does that make sense to come in for? I just really want to make sure I'm not coming across as disrespectful or disruptive to my team, you know?
Thinking back, did you have similar trouble sitting still or staying in your seat as a child, like in school, or is this something that's only started recently as an adult?

Um, well, I guess it isn't entirely new. I remember things sort of being this way for a long time, definitely way before high school. 

Back in elementary school, my teachers were always really nice and would write on my report cards that I was a bright student, which was really sweet of them. But... they did usually add that I rushed through my work a little too much. And, um, I guess I had a bit of a habit of talking out of turn? I never meant to be a bother or interrupt anyone, I think I just got a little too eager to participate. 

I also forgot my homework sometimes, and if you looked in my desk, it was usually just... stuffed with all these half-finished papers. It was a little embarrassing, honestly, but I really did try my best to keep it clean. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you currently notice ongoing problems with things like losing focus during tasks, forgetting appointments or details, or trouble staying organized in your day-to-day work?

Um, well... I guess I do have a little bit of trouble with the organization part. I mean, I always make sure my clients are taken care of! I really try my best to be on top of things. But behind the scenes, my system is maybe a little... messy? 

Like, my campaign notes will somehow end up split between my emails, a bunch of sticky notes on my desk, my actual planner, and just... random tabs left open on my computer. I know it sounds a little silly, and I'm really trying to find a better method, but because it's so spread out, I end up wasting a lot of time just trying to figure out what to do first instead of actually just starting the work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible at my job... I really do care about my work. Is that the kind of example you were looking for?
In your current daily life, do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, finishing other people's sentences, or having trouble waiting your turn when talking with colleagues or in meetings?

Um, I guess... maybe sometimes? I really, really try to be respectful of everyone's time and ideas, I promise. But, um, occasionally... if we're going through a pitch deck and someone is presenting, and I just get this really exciting idea that I think could help the campaign... I might sort of jump in? 

Like, I'll just pop over to their desk later or kind of chime in during a conversation to share my thought. I know I probably should just write it down and wait for a better moment, and I always feel a little bad if I accidentally cut someone off. I just get so enthusiastic about helping the team succeed, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound rude... I really don't mean to be. Does that make sense, or is that just a normal thing when you're brainstorming?
Do you notice similar difficulties—like restlessness, trouble organizing, or interrupting—in other areas of your life outside of work, such as at home or with friends and family?

Um, I don't really think so? I mean, I try really hard to keep things nice at home. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, so I always try to be a good listener with my friends and my boyfriend. 

I guess... maybe my apartment gets a little bit cluttered sometimes? But nothing crazy, just, you know, normal life stuff like mail on the counter or laundry waiting to be folded. And I really do try to stay on top of it. I don't think my friends would say I'm restless or anything... we mostly just hang out and watch movies or get dinner, and I'm totally fine just relaxing with them. 

So, yeah, I think it's mostly just work where I get a little scattered. Is it normal for it to just happen at work? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
{"intent": "Assess whether hyperactivity/impulsivity symptoms are pervasive across settings (

Um, no... I really don't think so. Like I said, I try so hard to be considerate when I'm not at work. I mean, my boyfriend and I have a really good relationship, and I always make sure to let him finish what he's saying. I really don't want to be one of those people who just talks over everyone. 

And as for feeling restless... I mean, sometimes after a long day at the office, I might fidget a tiny bit if we're watching a really long movie? But I think everyone does that, right? I mostly just try to be present and, you know, easygoing when I'm with my friends and family. I really want them to enjoy being around me. 

So, no, I don't think I'm impulsive or hyper at home... at least, I really hope I'm not. Do you think it's possible to just be a little scattered at work because it's so fast-paced?

Can you tell me about the last time you had to sit through something long at home—like a family dinner, a lecture, or a movie—did you notice yourself needing to get up, shift around, or leave the room at any point?

Um, well... we actually just watched this really long documentary the other night. My boyfriend loves them. And, um, I guess I did get up a couple of times? But it was just to, you know, get us some water and check if the dryer was done. I really just wanted to be helpful and make sure everything was taken care of so we could relax. 

I might have shifted around on the couch a little bit, but the cushions are kind of old and not that comfortable, so I think anyone would have needed to adjust. I definitely didn't leave the room just because I couldn't sit still or anything like that. I really try to be a good sport and watch what he likes. 

Does that sound okay? I mean, getting up to do a quick chore during a movie is pretty normal, isn't it? I just like to keep things nice for us.
Has your boyfriend, family, or close friends ever mentioned or teased you about being restless, distractible, or interrupting them, even if you didn't feel that way yourself?

Um, no, I don't think so? I mean, my boyfriend is really sweet, he wouldn't say anything mean like that. Sometimes he'll joke that I'm his little multitasker because I try to do a few things at once, like folding laundry while we talk, but he says he appreciates how much I get done. 

And my friends... they mostly just say I'm energetic, you know? Like I'm always up for doing something fun. I don't think anyone has ever complained about me interrupting or not paying attention. I try really, really hard to be a good friend and listen when they need to vent. 

I mean, if they did feel that way, I'd feel terrible. But no one has ever sat me down and told me I'm too much or anything. That would mean I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure I'm being a good partner and friend.

Has this pattern at work—getting up during meetings, jumping between different notes, or interrupting—ever actually affected your performance reviews, deadlines, or led to any formal feedback from your manager?

Um... well... I guess, maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try my best, I promise I do. I put so much effort into my job because I want my manager to be happy with my work. 

But, um... it has kind of come up in a performance review recently. Just... just a little note about needing to be more focused during client calls. And... there was this one time, a client actually said something to my boss about me interrupting and seeming distracted. It honestly broke my heart because I care so much about doing a good job for them. I would never intentionally be rude to a client, you know? 

I just... I get so eager to share an idea that I jump in too fast, or I'm trying to cross-reference my notes to be helpful and it comes off wrong. I'm really worried that I might damage an account, even though I'm trying so hard to be good at what I do. 

Does that make sense? I'm not a bad employee, right? I just... I really want to fix this so they know how much I care.
